analysis: The 16-negative SASRec cross-entropy trial completed successfully but reduced host validation macro HR@10 from the supplied prior 0.6250 to 0.6162, a drop of 0.0088. Category HR@10 was 0.635 for Movies_and_TV, 0.655 for Industrial_and_Scientific, 0.485 for Electronics, and 0.690 for CDs_and_Vinyl. Electronics had the lowest absolute score; prior category scores and current member scores were not supplied, so category regressions and individual expert contributions cannot be identified. The result does not support replacing one-negative BCE with this 16-negative objective in the retained ensemble. A possible explanation is changed SASRec rankings or reduced complementarity with MultVAE, but the available metrics do not establish the cause. The trial consumed 2007.12 allocated GPU-seconds.
code_summary: Retained four dataset-specific residual MultVAE–SASRec ensembles. MultVAE uses normalized binary histories, a 256-unit encoder, 64-dimensional variational latent, and a decoder hidden representation with an encoder residual; training retains multinomial reconstruction plus annealed KL. SASRec retains its default 200-position, 50-dimensional, two-block, one-head architecture with dropout 0.5. Its sampler now draws 16 uniform negatives with replacement per active transition, excluding the complete training history. Training gathers active features before negative embedding lookup and applies temperature-1 cross-entropy over one positive and 16 negatives. Inference retains equal-weight normalized mean-rank fusion, dataset routing, saved constructor configurations, and the generated predictor. Code includes isolated synthetic objective checks, checkpoint reload checks, fusion checks, and predictor parity checks.
